history-of-the-united-netherlands-1586e:
Chapters eleven and twelve of John Lothrop Motley's History of the United Netherlands bring Drake into the story. Sir Francis Drake's visit heartens the Dutch, and the Babington plot against Elizabeth darkens England's year. Leicester's absence leaves an ill-timed interregnum in the provinces. Factions grow during his government, and Motley anatomizes them.

The democratic theories of the Leicestrians meet the States' constitutional caution. Calvinist ambition for political power alarms the regents, who incline to tolerance. Motley contrasts desolation in the obedient provinces with prosperity in the republic. Pauperism and famine rule one side of the line; trade rules the other. The year of expectation, 1586, closes in suspense. These chapters are rich in the political ideas of the revolt, argued in pulpits, pamphlets, and council rooms.
podcast-dannyjones-Gmz2gphuw6E:
Physicist Jack Sarfatti returns to Danny Jones's podcast to argue that aerospace scientists are simply wrong about UFOs, because they refuse the physics he says explains them. Sarfatti presents his account of how the craft move, drawing on his decades of work at the edge of mainstream theory.

Jones gives him the technical floor, and Sarfatti uses it to attack the profession that ignores him. His claims are not accepted physics, and the episode does not pretend the journals agree with him. What it records is a working theorist's rebellion in his own voice: part physics lecture, part score-settling with an establishment he believes fears his conclusions. Listeners fascinated by the UFO question's scientific fringe get its most credentialed dissident, unfiltered and at length.
